title: SPEC A implementation: config staging/live promotion

completion_criteria.text: The seven unit PRs are all on main: five merged into stack parents rather than main and were re-integrated bottom-up through two further pr.mjs PRs, verified by merge-base ancestry.
SPEC A section 7's five cutover preconditions are all closed and verified, with the *session* gitignore pattern narrowed BEFORE the hook file it hides is adopted.
The promote verb is implemented with pre-swap validation, rollback by rename, and the LIVE receipt, and the bootstrap resolves outside releases/.
SessionStart and Stop converge hooks are registered, and a drift report reaches session context when live differs from main.
The settings.json ownership manifest and the separate capture verb are implemented, with unknown keys defaulting to LIVE WINS and flagged rather than dropped.
The cutover runs serially in a session doing nothing else: the first release is built and validated with zero live change, then every entry link is swapped in one pass.
All 10 of SPEC A's acceptance criteria pass, with criterion 10 verified by diffing the live tree against the release rather than asserted.
Every unit ships through a PR opened by pr.mjs pr-create, stacked with --base <parent-branch> where one change blocks another.

spine.active_goal: Ship SPEC A: the units are merged to main; what remains is two release-rejecting validation defects and then the cutover to immutable releases behind an atomic pointer.
spine.next_step: START HERE FRESH, in a session doing nothing else. 1) Land F1+F2+F3 via pr.mjs: drop notes from PROMOTED_ENTRIES, dispatch the hook syntax check on the shebang not the extension, keep settings.json out of the archive. 2) Re-run the faithful scratch rehearsal per 0281 until it reports promoted. 3) Cut over: fast-forward main, install the bootstrap in ~/.claude/local/, move notes/ there, delete the legacy graphify-out trees, build and validate the real release, swap only on explicit user go.
spine.last_session: Shipped seven unit PRs through a 13-agent workflow, repaired the stack's merge topology with two more PRs so all seven reached main at b24b266, then rehearsed the cutover and stopped: validation rejects every candidate on two real defects. Nothing live was touched.

open_risks.text: Serialize every write to a live-linked path, not just the cutover — the graphify hook edits and the converge-hook registration reach running sessions through the 26 hook symlinks, so a half-saved file breaks every session instantly.

Run the cutover serially in a session doing nothing else — it hot-swaps live-linked hooks, lib and workflows, so parallel subagents editing those paths can break every running session including the one doing the work.

Land the two release-rejecting defects before any cutover attempt — PROMOTED_ENTRIES still lists notes and the hook syntax check dispatches on the .sh extension, so validation rejects every candidate release permanently.

SPEC section 2 is stale against 0276 and the staleness is now in code — it draws eleven entry links including notes, which is how notes reached PROMOTED_ENTRIES; acceptance criterion 10's diff must also exclude local/ or it fails for the wrong reason.
Pass --ref origin/main or fast-forward local main first — local main sits at 0451220 while origin/main is b24b266, so a release built from the default ref ships the wrong tree.

Close every other claude session before the pointer swap — SPEC section 9 records that whether a swap reaches an already-running session is unmeasured, so any open session is an uncontrolled experiment on global config.
Never git checkout main in the primary checkout — live global config is 37 symlinks into that working tree, so switching branches hot-swaps every skill and hook under every running session.

Repoint protect-claude-config.sh at the LIVE receipt's repo_root in the cutover change — it finds the checkout by realpath'ing ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, which after cutover lands in releases/<sha>, not a git worktree, so the guard drops to a textual heuristic.

The single npm test failure is environmental, not a regression — protect-claude-config.test.mjs asserts ~/.claude/settings.json is a symlink when it is a real file, and it skips on CI runners, so green CI plus this one local failure is the expected reading.

key_decisions.title: SPEC A is implemented and shipped by a dedicated small dynamic workflow, with stacked PRs for blocking changes
The workflow fan-out boundary is any write to a live-linked path, not the cutover alone
Three plans are scrubbed at source; notes/ is reclassified live-only and never enters a release
chore/config-drift is the stack root and the inert basis lands before SPEC A's units
The inert basis ships as one atomic change carrying its evaluator, never as registry data alone
The inert basis leaves this phase's critical path; it buys SPEC A's PRs nothing and is under an open BLOCK
Every cutover attempt rehearses the real promote verb against a scratch config root before any live write
Release validation fails closed on any registered hook it cannot verify
Three residual validator weaknesses are disclosed in the invariant record rather than fixed

out_of_scope: Building SPEC B Part IV's stacked-PR machinery to serve this work - stacking here is manual via the convention, and 0271 orders SPEC A to land before any SPEC B unit
Editing mitosis.js or the parallel engine, which SPEC B governs
